hooks.text: Sitting Bull saw the soldiers falling long before they arrived.
Custer rode into a trap his scouts begged him to avoid.
210 men were lost because a commander ignored a vision.

title: Why Did Custer Ignore the Warnings at Little Bighorn? ⚠️
description: George Custer's 7th Cavalry was annihilated after he ignored his scouts' warnings. This is how Sitting Bull's vision of falling soldiers came true.

beats.text: Sitting Bull saw the soldiers falling long before they arrived.
beats.visual: Portrait of Sitting Bull, Lakota spiritual leader, 1885

beats.text: In June 1876, George Custer rode toward the Little Bighorn.
beats.visual: George Armstrong Custer in cavalry uniform, Civil War photograph

beats.text: Crow scouts warned him that the village was unprecedented.
Custer ignored them, unaware a supporting army had already retreated.
beats.visual: General George Crook in military uniform, 1870s

beats.text: He split his regiment to prevent the families from scattering.
beats.visual: Military map showing troop movements at the Little Bighorn
queries: Battle of the Little Bighorn map

beats.text: A final desperate note begged for reinforcements that never came.
beats.visual: Photograph of the original handwritten note from Custer to Benteen

beats.text: Over 200 cavalrymen were annihilated on a ridge within an hour.
beats.visual: Last Stand Hill memorial obelisk at Little Bighorn Battlefield

beats.text: Sitting Bull's vision of falling soldiers had come true.
beats.visual: Sitting Bull standing with a pipe, archive photograph, 1881

better_than_last: Improving the hook-to-loop narrative by using Sitting Bull's prophetic vision as both the opening intrigue and the concluding payoff.
